protocol: 3 rounds x 3 proposals; one positive scoring winner at most per round

descriptor_candidates.name: confine_ratio_entropy
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss scales with the confinement ratio (accessible volume per unit adsorbate-contact surface, normalized by the pore-limiting diameter): frameworks with high Vol/(ASA·lsd_p) retain more gas-like entropy, so adding this ratio to the 14-input model lowers MAE(entropy loss/R) by ≥10% vs baseline; falsified if MAE increases or changes <2%.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Translational entropy loss arises when adsorbate motion is restricted between pore walls; the ratio of free volume to wall-contact area scaled by pore diameter is a first-order confinement-geometry measure. Inference from adsorption thermodynamics, not from supplied evidence.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Retrain the same nonlinear network with this descriptor added; if MAE of entropy loss/R does not decrease by at least 10% on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs, reject.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_anisotropy_entropy
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with combined shape anisotropy of the adsorbate (PMI3/PMI1) times its span-to-brutto-depth ratio (SPAN/PBF), because elongated molecules lose more rotational freedom in channels than in cages; this shape term adds predictive power beyond volumetric features, tested by ≥5% MAE reduction; falsified if the term is redundant with MW/Vol (no improvement).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Rotational and configurational entropy loss depends on anisotropy of the guest molecule relative to pore geometry, not just size; principal moment ratios encode anisotropy. Inference from statistical mechanics of confined rotation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the model with this descriptor fails to beat the 14-input baseline MAE by ≥5% via cross-validation, or permutation importance of the new term is near zero, reject.

descriptor_candidates.name: free_volume_density_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Framework-level free-volume–density interplay controls framework vibrational contribution to entropy loss: the product AV·density (a framework-fraction index on the source scale) divided by the largest free sphere diameter, combined with accessible area, captures cage-vs-channel entropy fingerprints; adding it improves MAE ≥8%; falsified if AV and density are already jointly exploited by the network so the re-expression yields no gain.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Cage frameworks (high AV, low density at fixed lsd_f) impose stiffer guest localization and larger entropy loss than open channels; combining accessible volume, source density, and pore diameter probes this partitioning. Density used only at its source numerical scale. Inference from framework-density–adsorption correlations reported in literature on zeolite void fractions.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor leaves MAE within ±2% of baseline and the descriptor's learned contribution is statistically insignificant, reject the framework-mechanism hypothesis.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_window_confine_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases when the pore-limiting (guest) diameter is much smaller than the largest free-sphere (framework) diameter, i.e., in windows-with-cages topologies where guests are locally trapped; the descriptor Vol/AV (framework bulk-to-accessible volume ratio) times (lsd_p/lsd_f)^2 captures this window-cage contrast. Adding it to the 14-input model should lower MAE(entropy loss/R) by ≥5% vs the current best (0.5534 in R units); falsified if MAE increases or changes <2%.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from adsorption thermodynamics: translational/vibrational entropy loss is largest where a guest must pass narrow windows into larger cages (cage-like zeolites such as LTA/CHA lose more entropy than straight-channel MFI-type systems for similar accessible volume). The ratio lsd_p/lsd_f is a dimensionless window-vs-cage contrast; Vol/AV contrasts total framework volume with accessible volume at source scale. No supplied evidence; purely mechanistic inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Retrain the identical nonlinear network with 15 inputs; require ≥5% MAE reduction on held-out pairs relative to the retained baseline AND positive permutation importance for this term. If MAE change is within ±2% or negative, reject the window-cage trapping hypothesis.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_curvature_tortuosity_term
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales positively with a combined molecular surface-area-to-volume shape factor (LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3), a sphericity-like index) times the PBF/SPAN compactness ratio: near-spherical, compact adsorbates pack efficiently in cages and lose more rotational/configurational entropy per contact, while elongated ones slide along channels retaining more freedom. Adding this term should reduce MAE by ≥4%; falsified if MW and Vol already fully encode this shape information so the gain is <2%.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from statistical mechanics of confined rotation and packing: the number of resolvable orientational states scales with molecular surface-to-volume ratio and compactness; higher sphericity means fewer favorable orientations against curved pore walls, hence larger rotational entropy loss. Established that sphericity/shape factors influence adsorption, but this specific combination is untested here; classified uncertain as to literature novelty.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: ≥4% held-out MAE reduction vs the retained 14-input baseline, and permutation importance of the term above that of a randomly permuted control (p<0.05 over retraining seeds). Reject if gain <2% or if the term's importance is statistically indistinguishable from noise.

descriptor_candidates.name: gravimetric_area_window_penalty
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Two regimes govern entropy loss: (i) a specific-contact regime where accessible surface per unit adsorbate mass (ASA/MW, gravimetric contact intensity) raises the number of frustrated adsorbate modes, and (ii) a steric regime where lsd_p ≪ lsd_f amplifies entropy loss in the fourth power of the diameter ratio. The additive descriptor tests whether these are separable contributions beyond what the network extracts from raw inputs; expected ≥5% MAE reduction, falsified if the network's nonlinear recombination of ASA, MW, lsd_p, lsd_f already saturates this information (change <2%).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: entropic penalties arise from both the extent of guest-wall contact (per unit adsorbate amount, hence ASA/MW at source scales) and the severity of steric confinement (nonlinear, high-power dependence on window-to-cage diameter ratio, reflecting a threshold-like onset of full orientational freezing). All quantities dimensionless or at source numerical scale; no unverified units assigned. No supplied evidence; mechanistic inference only.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Train the same network with 15 inputs; accept only if held-out MAE(entropy loss/R) drops ≥5% below 0.5534 AND ablation of this descriptor degrades MAE by ≥2%. If either condition fails, the separability hypothesis (contact term + threshold term as independent mechanisms) is rejected.

descriptor_candidates.name: dimensional_contact_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with the molecular surface-to-volume ratio raised to 3/2 power (LabuteASA^1.5/Vol is a dimensionally consistent surface-intensity index): guests with large contact surface per unit volume experience more frustrated translational/rotational modes inside pores, so adding this term to the 15-input model lowers MAE(entropy loss/R) by ≥4% vs the current best (0.5409); falsified if MAE change is within ±2%.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from statistical mechanics of confinement: the density of wall-adjacent configurations scales with surface-to-volume ratio; LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3)-type indices partially worked in round 2 (surface_curvature term gave small gain), suggesting a sharper nonlinear re-expression may extract additional signal. Purely mechanistic inference; no supplied evidence.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Retrain the identical nonlinear network with this descriptor added; accept only if held-out MAE(entropy loss/R) drops ≥4% below 0.5409 AND ablation of the descriptor degrades MAE by ≥2%. Reject if the gain is <2% or the descriptor's permutation importance is statistically indistinguishable from noise.

descriptor_candidates.name: window_to_area_asymmetry
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is maximized when the window-to-framework diameter gap (|lsd_f - lsd_p|) coincides with a high pore-volume-to-surface ratio (AV/ASA, i.e., deep pockets rather than shallow surfaces): large cages reachable only through narrow windows trap guests in few configurations. The product of the diameter gap and the volume-per-area index tests this joint (interaction, not additive) mechanism; expected ≥5% MAE reduction vs 0.5409; falsified if the network already saturates this interaction (change <2%).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: prior retained descriptors showed that both window-vs-cage contrast (lsd_p/lsd_f) and volume/area ratios carry marginal predictive signal; this proposal tests whether their interaction — narrow windows guarding large voids — is the true mechanistic driver rather than either alone. Mechanistic inference from adsorption thermodynamics of cage-type zeolites; no supplied evidence.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Retrain the same network with 16 inputs; require ≥5% held-out MAE reduction relative to 0.5409 AND positive permutation importance. Reject if MAE increases, changes <2%, or the interaction term's importance is insignificant across retraining seeds.

descriptor_candidates.name: inertia_pocket_stiffness
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss depends on the match between adsorbate mid-to-minor inertia anisotropy (PMI2/PMI1) and the geometric stiffness of the pore pocket (lsd_p / Vol^(1/3), window diameter relative to cage linear size): high anisotropy in tight pockets freezes two rotational degrees of freedom, amplifying entropy loss. Adding this shape-geometry coupling term should reduce MAE by ≥4% vs 0.5409; falsified if shape information in PMI inputs is already fully exploited (change <2%).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from rotational partition functions of confined molecules: a guest loses rotational entropy when its inertia tensor anisotropy aligns with tight, locally spherical confinements; previous anisotropy-only descriptor (round 1) showed a small gain, motivating a coupling with pocket stiffness rather than anisotropy alone. Purely mechanistic inference; no supplied evidence.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Accept only if held-out MAE(entropy loss/R) drops ≥4% below 0.5409 and ablation degrades MAE by ≥2%. Reject if the gain is <2% or the term is redundant with the retained pore_window_confine_index (mutual-information check with retained descriptors).
